answer: The cipher multiplier is published, charged in garden, and horizon lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 11 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4774 identities would post 1059 proofs and burn roughly 44 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
